status: Closed — ESLint generated-tree boundaries and regression verified 2026-09-05
area: Runtime cache files can enter the repository-wide ESLint source universe
finding: ATM commands write transient TypeScript extracts under .atm-runtime-cache, but the repository ESLint configuration did not exclude that runtime-only directory. A partially generated extract was then parsed as product source and blocked the required lint gate. The same lint run also exposed duplicate imports in tracked source files, but those are ordinary source defects; the governance defect is that a non-source cache can make lint nondeterministic with respect to the tracked tree.
expectedBehavior: Repository lint must evaluate tracked source and declared generated source only. ATM runtime cache directories are transient operational state and must be ignored explicitly, so an interrupted cache write cannot create a parser error in the product lint gate. Real tracked-source lint errors remain visible and fail the command normally.
evidenceOrRepro: On 2026-08-20, npm run lint failed first at .atm-runtime-cache/scope-add-extract.ts:16 with a TypeScript parser error. On 2026-09-05, the same generated-path class reproduced at atm-git-hooks-ixrqXB/host/**. The repair adds explicit ignores for both generated roots in eslint.config.mjs; tests/cli/eslint-generated-path-boundaries.test.ts was red before the change and green after it, and npm run lint then exited 0.
followUp: Generated runtime and hook-host trees are now excluded from repository-wide ESLint enumeration. Future generated roots must add a focused boundary regression rather than broadening source exclusions without evidence.
